title: Kahana vs WooCommerce: Hubs vs SKUs
excerpt: WooCommerce is wordPress ecommerce plugin, open storefronts including digital products. Kahana is marketplace discovery for curated hubs, not another SKU grid.

columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: ≈4.17M live WooCommerce stores globally; powers ~20–39% of ecommerce sites / ~30% of online stores worldwide.
Stores generate USD 30–35B annual GMV; platform-level revenue estimates ~USD 41.2M in 2026 (+47.7% from 2025).
12,600+ stores earn USD 100K+/year; 2,100+ earn USD 1M+/year; average order value ~USD 75–95.
6.3M active WordPress installs, 344M+ downloads, 800+ official extensions plus thousands of third-party plugins.

strengths.title: Deep integration with WordPress
strengths.detail: Ideal for content-led businesses adding ecommerce (courses, downloads, memberships, merch).

strengths.title: No core monthly SaaS fee
strengths.detail: Core plugin is free, mainly host + optional extensions, attractive for small businesses and indie creators.

strengths.title: Highly customizable and extensible
strengths.detail: Rich ecosystem for payments, shipping, marketing, subscriptions, bookings, and more.

strengths.title: Strong where content + commerce intersect
strengths.detail: Great for blogs, magazines, and creators who want storefronts tied to content and SEO.

weaknesses.title: Setup and maintenance complexity
weaknesses.detail: Requires managing hosting, performance, security, and extension compatibility, more technical than Shopify.

weaknesses.title: Plugin sprawl and fragility
weaknesses.detail: Heavy third-party plugin dependence can cause conflicts and harder upgrades.

weaknesses.title: Scaling challenges
weaknesses.detail: Very large stores or flash sales often need specialized hosting, caching, and optimization.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. WooCommerce is wordPress ecommerce plugin, open storefronts including digital products. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

WooCommerce is a free, open-source ecommerce plugin for WordPress that lets merchants turn their sites into online stores, selling physical and digital products with extensive extensions for payments, shipping, and marketing. Official site.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and WooCommerce side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On WooCommerce you can use Memberships and Storefronts as first-class product jobs. The SKU is the product: a file, a theme, a craft listing, or a store you already operate.

Using Kahana with WooCommerce

You can use both. WooCommerce keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep WooCommerce for SKUs you already sell well. Put the curated collection on Kahana: a public hub on Explore, Aura as signal, and Stripe when you want a second place people can find and pay.
